newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airlines in Germany call for lower airport charges.
newsitem.headline: Airlines in Germany call for lower airport charges.

text.p: The European Commission proposal for transparent EU airport charges does not reflect airline interests sufficiently, carriers in Germany said.

The Board of Airline Representatives in Germany (Barig), representing 102 airlines, said it supported the Commission proposals published in April on non-discrimination, cost-relatedness and transparency of airport charges.
But non-discrimination should cover all flights, not just intra-EU, and more medium-term setting of charges should be pursued, the Barig full board agreed late Thursday.

Barig chairman Joergen Moellegaard, who is also Scandinavian Airline System AS Germany and Austria director, told Reuters: "We welcome the Commission initiative as it is high time we have common rules. Too often we are forced to negotiate with monopolies."
But air fares and airline yields were falling while airport charges, which represented 5-10 percent of airline operating costs but outside their control, were rising, he added.
"Airport charges must be related to what the airlines can earn. Airlines want lower charges and the public needs lower charges," he said.
Barig said a proposed clause allowing "charges modulations" to reflect changes in airport demand and use would in particular abandon the only objective standard for a well-balanced charges structure.
The association called on the EU Commission to adopt its proposals as a regulation rather than as a directive to ensure early unification of a legal framework for airport charges.
